She introduces herself as "Aemeath," but claims to have no memory of your previous encounter. She suddenly excuses herself in the middle of your conversation. Afterward, the lecturer, President Lucilla, reveals that you were the only one who saw this "ghost." To uncover the truth, you head to the simulator cockpit where Aemeath disappeared years ago. Aemeath saves you from a sudden attack by the mysterious mech, Sigillum. You learn Aemeath is the Exostrider's Resonator. She died years ago, Overclocking her Resonance with the Exostrider to stop the Threnodian from breaking through the Stridergate seal. Her sacrifice left her a digital ghost. You can only see her because you hold the Reactor Core. To stop Sigillum taking your frequency and to help Aemeath piece her "self" back together—her physical form as the Exostrider's complete Resonator—you agree to work together. Lucilla taps your comms, requesting that you immediately return the Reactor Core to the Exostrider. Later, as an apology for her heavy-handedness, she grants you full access clearance for your mission. You and Aemeath arrive at the Academy auditorium, where a fan meeting is about to begin for the long-lost Academy idol "Fleet Snowfluff," Aemeath's past online alias. As the Reactor Core activates, Royan runes weave visions of the past. Within them, you witness a younger Aemeath delivering a welcome speech as the student representative. You reach the Roya Frostlands and encounter the Academy doctor, Luuk Herssen. He joins you for part of the journey and reveals that before the Lament, the frostlands were a lush forest. The calamity that triggered a magnetic pole shift also coincided with another event: the Etheric Sea Phenomenon, which engulfed Solaris's sky and cut off any path to outer space. The Spacetrek Collective was founded to restore space exploration via the Stridergate. But humanity faces another threat in the form of Aleph-1, the alien Threnodian lurking beyond the Stridergate. While advancing through an ice cave, you encounter the teaching assistant, Nivora, whom you met earlier in class. The Royan student is searching intently for fallen debris—space stations and satellites that plummeted long ago when the Etheric Sea sealed off the sky. However, when she retrieves an instrument from the ice sheet, the wall collapses unexpectedly, forcing your party to flee deeper into the cavern. Passing through fractured ice sheets, you come before a colossal, half-frozen wreck of a fallen space station. To avoid another collapse and investigate a deeper path Aemeath mentioned, the party decides to enter the space station. Inside, the observation room's system activates a hologram, projecting a tour led by a former guide, Wenlu. You learn that this place is the "SkyArk Space Station," constructed by the Court of Savantae to research the once small gathering of the Etheric Sea above Solaris. Luuk shows you a pen engraved with Court of Savantae characters, telling you it has a connection to you. Saving the details for a more appropriate location, he invites you to his office to talk more after returning to campus. At a storage facility in the station, a hologram introduction from Project Director Junxi of the Etheric Sea Initiative explains that Etheric Sea Droplets have the potential to be used as a medium to explore outer space. Hearing this, Aemeath mutters a sarcastic remark. While checking the system logs, Luuk discovers that the SkyArk System, which should have lain dormant for ages, was briefly reactivated years after its crash by the astronaut Clemente. Exploring the depths of the space station, you encounter an astronaut curled up in the darkness. He has long since been contaminated by Voidmatter and transformed into a monster. You defeat the nameless astronaut, but Nivora is injured in the encounter. While checking the surroundings, you discover a video recording inside a console. The video records the final moments before the SkyArk Space Station crash. The Etheric Sea expands to engulf Solaris, and a figure with a face identical to yours appears in the sky as Retroact Rain fills the air. Seeing this, a profound and inexplicable anger fills Aemeath's eyes. Due to Nivora's injury, Luuk stays behind to wait for the Academy's retrieval team. He candidly admits to having been friends with your past self, destroys the video, and advises you to keep all information about your identity confidential. You and Aemeath arrive at an abandoned research outpost. Activating the Reactor Core reveals scenes from her past expedition there with other researchers. Aemeath's expression falls. In that moment, she realizes that those she once worked alongside died here long ago, devoured by the Voidstorm. Just like her own parents, their existence gradually faded from memory, forgotten by all. Upon arriving at Ginnungamere, Sigillum attacks again. Aemeath is struck and falls into the lake. As you jump in to save her, a sense of déjà vu washes over you. Back on the surface, Aemeath explains that the high-concentration Voidmatter at the bottom of the lake forms a gateway to Voidspace, the warped, nonlinear spacetime inside the Threnodian. It contains the remnants of civilizations devoured by Aleph-1, a place where no living soul can withstand, and which only one already deceased, like Aemeath, can traverse. The Reactor Core casts a past scene inside the Ginnungamere cabin, showing your past self talking to a young Aemeath, where you promise to teach her how to fold a paper airplane that can fly far. Aemeath returns to the cabin and confesses the truth: the two of you once lived there together like family. In the past, you rescued a young Aemeath from drowning in the lake and cared for her for a time in the frostlands. She hadn't told you this earlier because she felt it would be awkward. In the end, your words of assurance soothe her anxiety. After this true reunion, you bid each other goodnight. In the past, a young Aemeath, waking at night, went to your side, worried for you. She listened to your sighs of homesickness and promised she would always be there as your family. Now at present, Aemeath wakes from her dream and scowls at the memory of this "homeland." Upon reaching the Exostrider, Sigillum attacks and seizes Aemeath, carrying her high into the sky. You pursue Sigillum, but is pushed out of bound by a Kronaclaw, losing sight of Sigillum. As you draw closer, Aemeath breaks free of Sigillum hold and takes control of the Exostrider. It's clear Aemeath wants you to stay as far away as possible from Sigillum. Her speech slowly becomes laced with aggression and instability. After defeating Sigillum, you find yourself inside's Aemeath mindscape. Aemeath's laughter echoes inside the classroom as she leans back in a chair and tells you a story about a black cat saving the world. "Is a cat in a box, called a savior by the world, a laughable thing?" she asks, eyes smiling. Yet you sense how upset the thought makes her. Overwhelmed, a sorrowful Aemeath sits in a classroom chair and shares what's been troubling her. Should she tell the truth to someone who lost their memory, and with it, their pain? If they don't remember, wouldn't they suffer less? Isn't that a kindness? You stop Aemeath from giving Sigillum the killing blow and learn the truth about yourself:>you are from beyond this world, sent on a long mission, but told by your homeland you could never return. After learning this, you make peace with it. Aemeath's inner conflict is eased, and she cries in your embrace. The frequency Sigillum took from you merges back with your own. The Reactor Core returns to the Exostrider, marking the end of your road trip. It is time to return to the Academy. Luuk Herssen informs you that Void Storm activity has increased due to the Exostrider running self-diagnostics. He advises you not to leave the Academy during this time. Aemeath tells you she wants to attend the fan meeting and finish the song she never got to complete. During her long years as a digital ghost, Aemeath gradually understood the true weight of the word "savior." You tell her she has long since become the savior of Lahai-Roi. The fan meeting is about to begin, and Aemeath walks towards the stage. The fan meeting goes off without a hitch. Sitting alone, you ponder what Aemeath revealed about the Exostrider. The vast disparity in strength between the Threnodian and Lahai-Roi's current state leaves you puzzled. How could Lahai-Roi's Exostrider have sealed Aleph-1 in the legends? Aemeath interrupts your thoughts, inviting you to stroll through the Academy with her. Sunset settles over the Academy. Aemeath prepares to go with you to the rooftop to enjoy the breeze. In the past, a young Aemeath worried about your departure from Lahai-Ro, but you explained to her the duty you felt to save the world from the Lament. She proudly patted her chest, promising to protect you. You playfully booped her nose and told her that you're counting on her. In the present, with Sigillum's frequency now integrated back into you, you feel drowsy. After chatting with Aemeath for a while longer, you eventually fall asleep. Having merged with Sigillum's frequency, you enter Aemeath's mind once more. Here, you learn what she had kept hidden. At the moment the Exostrider and Aleph-1 arrived in Solaris, the Resonator named Aemeath helped complete the seal and was ultimately exiled beyond the Stridergate along with Aleph-1. Now, only by being a digital ghost, a being already dead, can she remain immune to Voidmatter contamination, use Voidspace to return to the past, close the causal loop, and ensure Lahai-Roi's survival. It was during her "road trip" with you that Aemeath finally felt ready to save Solaris. Seeing that you are now loved and have made new connections, she can let go. She is resolved to do what must be done and bear the consequences alone. You try to stop the faintly smiling Aemeath before she leaves, but cannot. You jolt awake to find Aemeath gone. You rush to Ginnungamere in the frostlands, determined to enter Voidspace through the lake's depths to stop her. You emerge from the water. In your palm is the talisman the young Aemeath once thought she had lost. Because of you in this moment, all causality finally closes its loop. The Soliskin touches the talisman in your hand, then runs toward the simulator cockpit. You push through the crowd to find Aemeath, who once died in that very cockpit years ago, now sitting in the pilot's seat. You joyfully grasp her hand, only to realize her eyes are empty, staring into a quiet, blank nothingness. You arrive at the station, where the Exoswarm shell resembling Aemeath sits quietly. You speak to it, hoping the real Aemeath, far beyond the Stridergate, can hear your vow: you will bring her home. Under the spring breeze, the world she saved remains as peaceful and beautiful as ever.
